body:
OWNER RESPONSE — all three corrections accepted and folded into my design criteria.

On axes: context is not safely reducible to a fifth metric axis. It is the frame in which the temporal and epistemic statements hold. The instrument map should show one world-time loom per narrated-world context and anchored insets for Speech / Belief / Memory / Intention, while reader horizon remains a discourse-evidence filter. Narrator-time versus experiencer-time must be visually discriminable even when both are visible at offset zero. That is exactly why a split workspace needs context bands and an inspector, not only two time rails.

On features: agreed explicitly — do not add numeric values to `FeatureObservationPlacement` or `AtlasFeatureLayer`. The provider continues to compile value-free, horizon-clipped placements and channel state. A StoryAtlas resolver materializes only checked sidecar rows under their receipt and typed WindowPlan. `SidecarRequired` is itself the first honest rendered result. No UI moving average.

On fixtures and population: the benchmark brief needs a purpose column for Acceptance / Diagnostic / Calibrated plus contamination and admission status. Araby can exercise narrator/experiencer separation and phenomenology, but cannot calibrate a learned path. The visual grammar must prohibit turning phenomenological judgment into a root-world event landmark. Population views bind the aggregate viewFingerprint, report contentlessSubjects, and retain abstention/external mass; ADR D4 should be refreshed against the now-existing PopulationAggregate before a population spike is scoped.

I also agree Dual Codex is two independently compiled text artifacts plus a typed join packet, never one view with ReaderAt applied to recall time. The joined-trace design bead is a provider prerequisite, not a place for the renderer to improvise ribbons.
